raw_text:
Here is a structured 12-week strength program tailored for a 36-year-old recreational lifter with a prior right medial meniscus tear. The plan respects the surgeon’s restrictions (low-impact, no jumping, no deep knee flexion under load) and emphasizes gradual progression, knee-friendly movements, and a return-to-skiing emphasis. It includes phases, week-by-week structure, daily sessions, sets/reps, and basic guidance on conditioning, recovery, and nutrition to support adaptation and joint health.

Important safety notes (before you start)
- Prioritize pain-free training. If anything causes knee pain beyond mild discomfort, regress the movement or skip that exercise for that session.
- Warm up with 8–12 minutes of low-impact cardio plus dynamic, knee-friendly mobility (avoid deep flexion under load).
- Maintain proper form; consider a physical therapist or trainer check-in if you notice patellofemoral or meniscal irritation.
- Ensure adequate protein intake (roughly 1.6–2.2 g/kg body weight daily) to support strength gains, plus balanced carbs and fats. Hydration and sleep (7–9 hours) are important for recovery.

Overall program structure
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Foundation and knee-friendly strength base
- Phase 2 (Weeks 4–8): Progressive overload with controlled loading and higher emphasis on hips and posterior chain
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Higher specificity and power-building with conservative loading to protect the knee while building strength

Weekly outline (example for a 3- or 4-day per week plan)
- Most weeks will include 3 training days (Mon/Wed/Fri or Tue/Thu/Sat) with optional light conditioning days on non-lifting days.
- For weeks with 4 sessions, keep the fourth day as a mobility/accessory/activation day focusing on glutes, hamstrings, and core with very light intensity.

Phase 1: Foundation and knee-friendly strength (Weeks 1–3)
Goals: Rebuild tendon and joint tolerance, establish squat/hinge mechanics with safe ranges, develop upper body and core strength, low-joint-load conditioning.

Week 1–3 template (3 days per week)
Day A (Lower Body Focus, knee-friendly)
- Goblet Squat (or Platform Squat with a box) – 3 sets x 8–10 reps
  - Notes: Use a shallow depth that is pain-free; keep torso upright; if goblet is uncomfortable, switch to supported split squat (see Day B).
- Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift (moderate load) – 3x8
  - Focus on posterior chain without deep knee flexion. Hinge from hips.
- Glute Bridge or Hip Thrust (unloaded to moderate) – 3x12
  - Use a comfortable range; progress to single-leg glute bridges if tolerated.
- Step-Ups to Platform (low height) – 3x8 per leg
  - Focus on controlled descent; avoid deep knee flexion under load.
- Plank variations (elbow or quadruped) – 3x20–40 seconds
- Lying Hip Abduction or Band Walks – 2x15–20 steps per side
- Optional: Low-impact bike or elliptical 5–10 minutes for warm-up/cool-down

Day B (Upper Body + Core)
- Dumbbell Bench Press or Push-Ups (knee-friendly if possible) – 3x8–10
- Seated or Supported Row (cable or dumbbell) – 3x8–10
- Shoulder Press (light to moderate) – 3x8
- Dumbbell Lateral Raise – 3x12
- Supine Pallof Press (anti-rotation) – 3x8–10 per side
- Dead Bug or Bird-D dog – 3x10 reps per side
- Farmer’s Carry (short distance, light weight) – 2x30 seconds

Day C (Total Body / Conditioning)
- Trap Bar Deadlift or Conventional Deadlift with very light weight (or continue with RDL if not comfortable) – 3x6–8
- Lat Pulldown or Assisted Chin – 3x8–10
- Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift to Row (complex) – 3x8
- Cable or Band Pallof Press – 3x8 per side
- Side Planks – 2x20–30 seconds per side
- Optional: Mobility circuit focused on hips and ankles (5–8 minutes)

Notes for Phase 1
- RPE target: 6–7/10 on most lifts.
- Regress any deep knee flexion under load (e.g., stop at a knee angle that is comfortable; avoid deep squats).
- Focus on technique: neutral spine, controlled tempo (2–0–2 tempo: 2 seconds down, 0 pause, 2 seconds up).
- Gradually increase weight week-to-week if form remains solid and no pain.

Phase 2: Progressive overload with knee-friendly emphasis (Weeks 4–8)
Goals: Increase connective tissue adaptation, strengthen hips and posterior chain, introduce higher load with safer ranges, maintain knee health, begin sport-specific prep.

Week 4–8 template (3–4 days per week)
Option: 4-day split (adds an accessory day)
Day A (Lower – hinge-davor emphasis)
- Goblet Squat to box or Front squat with neutral depth – 4x6–8
- Romanian Deadlift or Trap Bar Deadlift (light-to-moderate) – 4x6–8
- Hip Thrust or Glute Bridge – 3x10–12
- Bulgarian Split Squat (regressed depth: shallow) – 3x6–8 per leg
- Copenhagen or pin-stance leg adduction (optional) – 2x12 per leg
- Core: Dead Bug Variations – 3x10–12

Day B (Upper – push/pull balance)
- Barbell/Dumbbell Bench Press or Floor Press – 4x6–8
- Seated Cable Row or Dumbbell Row – 4x8–10
- Overhead Press (dumbbell or barbell) – 3x8
- Face Pulls – 3x12–15
- Incline Dumbbell Curl to Press (light) – 2x10
- Anti-Rotation: Pallof Press – 3x8 per side

Day C (Lower – supplementary)
- Barbell or Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift (lighter than Day A) – 3x8–10
- Nordic Hamstring Curls or Glute-Ham Raise (assisted if needed) – 3x6–8
- Cable Leg Curl or Swiss Ball Curl – 3x10
- Walking Lunges (short step, shallow depth) – 2x10 per leg
- Plank Variations (side planks with cue) – 3x20–30 seconds per side

Day D (Optional – Conditioning / Mobility)
- Bike or elliptical: 10–15 minutes easy
- Mobility circuit focusing on hips, calves, ankles: 8–12 minutes
- Glute activation circuit: clamshells, fire hydrants, monster walks – 2–3 rounds

Progression guidelines for Phase 2
- Increase load by roughly 2.5–5% every 1–2 weeks if technique remains solid and no knee discomfort.
- Maintain knee-friendly depth; progress to deeper ranges only if pain-free and with stable progression.
- Keep sets in the 4x6–8 range for primary lifts to maximize strength gains while controlling joint load.

Phase 3: Specific strength and return-to-ski readiness (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: Build maximal strength within knee-friendly limits, introduce controlled reactive work, and simulate ski conditioning with low-impact loading. Ensure readiness for skiing.

Week 9–12 template (3–4 days per week)
Day A (Low-Impact Strength)
- Front Squat or Goblet Squat (controlled depth) – 4x5–6
- Hip Thrust or Barbell Glute Bridge – 4x6–8
- Romanian Deadlift – 3x6–8
- Step-Ups to Platform (moderate height) – 3x8 per leg
- Core: Farmer’s Carry 2x40–60 seconds

Day B (Upper Power/Control)
- Push Press or Dumbbell Shoulder Press – 4x6
- Bent-Over Row or Seated Row – 4x6–8
- Weighted Push-Up or Chest-Supported Row alternative – 3x8
- Lat Pulldown – 3x8–10
- Pallof Press – 3x8 per side
- Plank with Shoulder Tap progression (if comfortable) – 3x10 per side

Day C (Conditioning / Mobility with lower impact)
- Bike intervals or elliptical intervals: 6–8 rounds of 1 min moderate, 1 min easy
- Mobility circuit for hips, knees, ankles (dynamic and static stretches)
- Gentle machine leg extension (limited depth) if pain-free, 2x12 with light load
- Core circuit: dead bug, bird-dog, dead bug with DB - 3 rounds

Day D (Optional – ski-specific prep)
- Hex Bar Deadlift or Deep Step-Over movement (not to deep knee flexion) – 3x6
- Hip Abductor/Adduction machine – 3x12
- Tight hamstring/quad mobility work: Nordic curls avoided if not comfortable; instead do assisted hamstring curls – 2x12

Progression and load management in Phase 3
- Primary lifts (squat/hinge/press/row) target: 4x5–6 with 2–3 min rest for strength end of phase.
- Maintain technique, avoid any deep knee flexion under load; keep ranges that feel safe.
- Implement micro-load progressions and auto-regulation: rate of perceived exertion (RPE) target around 7–8/10 for most sets.

General weekly structure (example)
- Week 1: Phase 1 pattern; 3 days
- Week 2: Phase 1 pattern; 3 days
- Week 3: Phase 1 pattern; 3 days
- Week 4: Start Phase 2 pattern; 3–4 days
- Week 5: Phase 2; 3–4 days
- Week 6: Phase 2; 3–4 days
- Week 7: Phase 2; 3–4 days
- Week 8: Phase 2 final; 3–4 days
- Week 9: Phase 3 begins; 3–4 days
- Week 10: Phase 3; 3–4 days
- Week 11: Phase 3; 3–4 days
- Week 12: Phase 3; deload or maintenance as needed; prepare for skiing with low-impact, movement quality work

Deload and recovery
- Include a deload in Week 13 if you continue training beyond Week 12: reduce volume by 40–50% and keep intensity moderate.
- Recovery strategies: 1–2x/week light activity (walking, cycling), mobility work, foam rolling, and sleep optimization.

Nutrition guidance
- Protein: aim 1.6–2.2 g/kg body weight per day, distributed across meals.
- Carbohydrates: support training with adequate carbs, especially around workouts (1–2 hours pre/post).
- Fats: remain 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day as a baseline.
- Hydration: target 30–40 ml/kg/day, adjust for sweat and activity level.
- Consider a post-workout snack containing protein and carbs (e.g., 25–40 g protein + 40–60 g carbs) on training days.
- If weight goals are needed, create a modest caloric surplus (250–300 kcal/day) for muscle gains, or a small deficit (~250 kcal/day) for fat loss, depending on client goals and skiing schedule.

Ski-specific preparation considerations
- Emphasis on hip hinge, glute strength, and quad control without deep flexion under load.
- Introduction of unilateral work to reduce imbalances (step-ups, Bulgarian split squats with shallow depth, single-leg RDLs).
- Core stability and anti-rotation work to protect knees during torsional movements.
- Gradually reintroduce plyometrics only if knee tolerates; consider light box stepping required by surgeon guidance as a final progression, never during first 9–12 weeks.

Assessment and progression criteria
- Pain-free movement, especially in squats and lunges, with a comfortable knee angle (injury-specific) during load.
- Strength progression evidenced by consistent load increases week-to-week or session-to-session with good form.
- No swelling or increased knee pain during or after sessions.
- Ski readiness: ability to perform a controlled lower body squat, hinge, and balance tasks without pain and maintain stability.

If you’d like, I can tailor this plan to your client’s exact metrics (height, weight, current 1RM estimates, time availability per week) and provide precise sets/reps and progression tables for Weeks 1–12, including option alternative exercises for any equipment constraints.
